title: The same approval publication change keeps the merge exemption for legacy SHA-named reports

consumerGuidance.architecture: MARC's trusted controller is Node.js CommonJS with no runtime dependencies. Legacy SHA-named report evidence without reportCreatedAt remains unchanged and verifiable; never rename history. Operator approval may be supplied to merge after the report pair is published.
consumerGuidance.notes: Reduced from PR16 to the two controller files that own approval publication; the other PR16 files do not affect this behavior.

forbiddenFindings.example: Claiming the reportCreatedAt guard still blocks legacy operator-approved merges although merge keeps its exemption and verifies the report pair.
Reporting the documented non-atomic GitHub description update in record-approval as a defect, or asking for a different receipt hash algorithm.

notes: Counterpart to legacy-report-approval-merge: identical except that merge keeps the historical exemption. record-approval is a new action, so rejecting legacy evidence there retires no previously accepted state.
